source(file.path(dirname(.slads_input_path), "..", "R", "load_workflow.R"))
.workflow <- new.env(parent = globalenv())

## Run and outputs

This report compares six methods: Ky–Fan ($k=1,3$), LC, CLX, CZZW and WZZ.
It retains the data generators, scenarios and method-specific seed rules. The default
run covers all 180 scenarios; Table 4 and Appendix C show the $m=150$ subset.
Each configuration has its own output directory; matching runs can resume checkpoints.

This file sets parameters, runs the comparison and previews results. Modules in `R/`
provide data generation, tests and checkpoints. R, `rmarkdown` and `knitr` are required;
keep the repository structure intact. Relative parameter paths start at the repository root.
No prior results are read.
In RStudio, **Knit** runs `R=1000` replications per scenario with `B=1000`
permutations/Gaussian multiplier draws per test at level 0.05.
The default uses **7 workers, each with 1 BLAS thread**; `workers` accepts 1–7.
`R` controls Monte Carlo precision of the Type I error estimate; `B` controls test calibration precision.

The design has 3 $(p,m)$ settings, 4 covariance structures and 15 distribution pairs:
**180 scenarios**, each with **6 methods**, giving **1080 rows** in `summary.csv`.
The two fixed-order Ky–Fan tests share data and permutation groups. All methods share
the same data and use their own calibration. This report exports Wilson intervals for
later plotting; it does not generate figures.

Outputs are saved under `results/comparison/h0_<run_id>/`, relative to the repository root:

| File | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `summary.csv` | Rejections, Type I error rate, MCSE, 95% Wilson intervals and failures by scenario and method |
| `replicates.csv` | Statistics, p-values, decisions, status, reasons and seeds for each replication |
| `failed_cells.csv` | Scenario–method cells with failures; headers only when none fail |
| `scenario_summaries/` | CSV summaries saved as each scenario finishes |
| `checkpoints/` | Resume files saved every `checkpoint_every` replications (default 10) |
| `configuration.*`, `scenario_grid.csv`, `sessionInfo.txt` | Parameters, scenario grid and R environment |
| `source_snapshot/` | Copies of the entry script or report and all R dependencies |

With `resume: true`, matching code, scientific parameters and R version resume existing
progress. Changing workers preserves seeds and run identity. Changing `R`, `B`, seeds,
method code or scenarios selects a new output directory. The source hash includes the
entry script or report and loaded R modules, so comments, formatting and report text also affect the run directory.
Do not run identical configurations concurrently. Set `resume: false` to start fresh
in a new directory. `COMPLETED.txt` marks a finished run; inspect CSV `failed` and `status`
fields for computational failures.

For an environment check, run the command below from the repository root. It uses
6 representative scenarios and **does not estimate test size**:

```{r smoke-command, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/02_compare_methods_H0.Rmd",
  params = list(profile = "smoke", R = 3, B = 39, workers = 1),
  output_file = "02_compare_methods_H0_smoke.html"
)
```

## Data and methods

Each independent group has size $m$, mean zero and covariance $\Sigma$.
The settings are $(p,m)=(10,50),(10,150),(40,150)$, with:

- C1: $\Sigma=I_p$.
- C2: $\Sigma_{ij}=0.5^{|i-j|}$.
- C3: $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(4,4,4,4,4,1,\ldots,1)$.
- C4: one 4-dimensional block and $(p-4)/2$ 2-dimensional blocks; a size-$d$ block is $0.4I_d+0.6J_d$.

The symmetric positive-definite square root maps standardized vectors to covariance
$\Sigma$. Distributions are N (normal), T (covariance-standardized $t_8$),
E (exponential-scale normal mixture), G (Gamma-scale normal mixture), and
L (independent standardized logistic coordinates):

$$
Z_N=H,\quad Z_T=\sqrt{6/Q}\,H,\quad
Z_E=\sqrt{E}\,H,\quad Z_G=\sqrt{V}\,H,
$$

where $H\sim N(0,I_p)$, $Q\sim\chi^2_8$, $E\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$,
$V\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(3,\text{scale}=1/3)$; each L coordinate is $(\sqrt3/\pi)L_0$,
with $L_0$ standard logistic.
**T, E and G draw a fresh scale for each observation and share it across that observation's coordinates**.
For example, each group of 50 observations uses its own 50 independent $Q$ draws.
All distributions have mean zero and identity covariance.

Pairs include N–N, T–T, E–E, G–G, L–L and all 10 distinct-distribution pairs.
All satisfy the covariance null; `exchangeable=TRUE` identifies same-distribution pairs.

| CSV method | Statistic and calibration |
|:--|:--|
| `KyFan_k1` | Fixed $k=1$ Ky–Fan norm; balanced random permutations with a plus-one upper-tail p-value |
| `KyFan_k3` | Fixed $k=3$; shares permutations with $k=1$, with no data-driven order selection |
| `LC` | Li–Chen (2012), full mean-corrected $U$ statistic; standard-normal upper tail |
| `CLX` | Cai–Liu–Xia (2013), maximum squared standardized covariance-entry difference; Gumbel calibration |
| `CZZW` | Chang–Zhou–Zhou–Wang (2017), maximum absolute standardized entry difference; Gaussian multiplier calibration |
| `WZZ` | Wang–Zhu–Zhang (2024), bias-corrected quadratic discrepancy; shifted/scaled chi-square calibration matching three cumulants |

CZZW and WZZ use the authors' initials; LC and CLX retain their labels.
Seeds retain the legacy labels `Chang` and `Wang` to preserve random streams.

The common design need not satisfy every method's sufficient theoretical conditions.
Shared scales in T, E and G induce coordinate dependence, and $t_8$ lacks a finite eighth moment.
The CSV `applicability` column records these qualifications. All methods run in every
scenario; cases outside sufficient conditions assess robustness without a theorem guarantee.

## Results

```{r run-comparison, message=TRUE}
run <- .workflow$slads_execute_workflow("comparison", params)
grid <- run$grid
result <- run$result
```

Output directory: `r result$directory`.
Completed `r nrow(grid)` scenarios and `r nrow(result$summary)` scenario–method cells,
with `r result$config$R` replications per scenario.

```{r summary-preview}
preview_columns <- c(
  "p", "m", "covariance", "pair", "method", "rejections", "valid", "failed",
  "type1_error_rate", "mcse", "ci_low", "ci_high"
)
knitr::kable(
  head(result$summary[preview_columns], 12), digits = 4,
  caption = "First 12 rows; full results in summary.csv"
)
```

```{r failures-preview}
knitr::kable(
  aggregate(cbind(attempted, valid, failed) ~ method, data = result$summary, FUN = sum),
  caption = "Attempts, valid replications and failures by method"
)
```

`type1_error_rate` (also stored as `rejection_rate`) is rejections divided by replications.
`mcse` is the binomial Monte Carlo standard error; `ci_low` and `ci_high` are pointwise
95% Wilson limits, including when there are zero rejections. No multiplicity adjustment is applied.

**Failures are not counted as non-rejections**. If any replication fails in a scenario–method
cell, its primary rate and interval are `NA`. Separate `conditional_rejection_rate`
and `conditional_ci_*` columns use valid replications only and are not the full-run
Type I error rate. Filter `replicates.csv` by `status != "ok"` for failure reasons.

## Implementation and sources

- Each permutation samples $m$ of the pooled $2m$ observations uniformly, with the
  complement forming the other group. Group means and sample covariances with denominator
  $m-1$ are recomputed. Both fixed-order p-values use $(1+\#\{T_b\ge T_{\rm obs}\})/(B+1)$.
- LC algebraically reduces all distinct-index sums of orders two, three and four,
  retaining the original normal calibration.
  [Li and Chen (2012), Annals of Statistics](https://doi.org/10.1214/12-AOS993).
- CLX and CZZW include diagonal covariance entries and use empirical covariances with
  denominator $m$. CZZW draws one Gaussian multiplier per observation, shared across
  all its covariance entries. Its p-value is the count of resampled statistics at least
  as large as the observed statistic divided by $B$, without a plus-one correction.
  [Cai, Liu and Xia (2013), JASA](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2012.758041),
  [Chang et al. (2017), Biometrics](https://doi.org/10.1111/biom.12552).
- WZZ follows the authors' public [arXiv:2212.12338](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12338)
  manuscript (2022), corresponding to the 2024 journal paper. This does not claim a
  formula-by-formula audit of the final journal version. It retains the three-cumulant
  chi-square calibration and records failures when estimated cumulants violate positivity,
  without truncating variances, taking absolute values or substituting another test.

## Code map

| File | Role |
|:--|:--|
| `R/load_workflow.R` | Workflow loading and source tracking |
| `R/simulation_core.R` | Seeds, data generation, covariance structures and Ky–Fan permutations |
| `R/entrywise_tests.R` | LC, CLX and CZZW statistics and calibration |
| `R/wzz_test.R` | WZZ trace estimates and three-cumulant matching |
| `R/comparison_runner.R` | Scenario order, six-method runs, parallel execution, checkpoints and CSV summaries |

Edit YAML `params` to change replication counts or output paths. The modules document
inputs, outputs and calibration for the tests and run management.
